chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Razin, who said:

Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih handed over to me some dirhams from the zakat to distribute. So I came to him one day and he asked me, 'Did you distribute them?' So I said, 'No'. So he made me listen to words wherein was some harshness. So I dropped what remained with me from the dirhams and I arose in anger. So he said to me, 'Return, until I narrate to you something which I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)'. So I returned. So he said, 'I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When I find my zakat, I take it out and hand it over to one whom I trust to distribute it'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with that. Indeed, he is one of the givers'.
Salih said, 'So I took the dirhams when I heard the hadith, and I distributed them'.

key_terms.أَحَدُ الْمُعْطِينَ: One of the givers (participants in reward)

ai.seo_question: Can I give my zakat to someone else to distribute on my behalf?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia legal principle of delegating zakat distribution to a trustworthy agent (muqassim), emphasizing that the trustee shares in the spiritual reward as a co-donor. The Imam’s confirmation that the trustee is 'one of the givers' underscores the continuity of reward through agency, a concept rooted in the broader Shia jurisprudence of trust (amanah) and the merit of charitable intermediaries.
